sections_read: Introduction: unrestricted Koebe statement, two component obstructions, finite approximation context, proof overview and classical inputs
The quotient sphere and compatible coordinates: Moore quotient, dust disks/contours and exhaustion, bands and masks, compatibility(P), generic level continua, null trace-image criterion

Finite transfer and normalized limits: random staircases, grid and terminal-index selection, rank-one fillings, common metric optimization, finite circle-domain uniformization, normalized compactness, end correspondence and disk trapping

Tagged paths and compatible barriers: repeated-visit costs, tag/residual incidence constraints, restriction and countable concatenation, Borel coding, collar splicing, shrinking-jump removal, chain distance, band-preserving smoothing and compatibility

Positive laws of admissible paths: pointwise extended-density modulus duality, prescribed-countable and atomless tests, weighted tuple measures, fusion from countable tests to counting l2 on the whole dust, application to candidate path laws

The first selection and path–level intersections: domain-point avoidance, diffuse dust-intersection removal, four-path crossing, countability of unavailable ends, maximal compatible barrier selection, parallel-line payment, unmarked collapse, generic prior-level intersections

Period coordinates and marked components: compact simple-arc reduction, lifted ray indices, average period-one coordinate, occupation energy/bands/positive boundary measure/compatibility/smoothing, Stokes upper bound, local bad-pair exclusion, retained-test selection, main theorem and scalar retained-test corollary
A hyperbolic convex-hull realization: genus-zero complete curvature -1 corollary and its stated limits
Both complete included TikZ figures (protrusion and four-path crossing), complete bibliography, README and main TeX
claim_as_stated: The source asserts that every nonempty connected open subset G of the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a circle domain, with no countability, regularity, or separation assumption on its complementary components. Its stronger retained-test theorem preserves an arbitrary countable well-ordered compatible list, exactly on exhausting compact cores, with vanishing total added Dirichlet energy and vanishing counting-l2 positive-excess boundary oscillations, and supplies a countable persistent extension all of whose diagonal finite-transfer limits have circle-domain image. A corollary, using Luo–Wu, realizes every orientable complete genus-zero curvature -1 surface as the intrinsic boundary of a hyperbolic convex hull of a compact circle-type ideal set; it claims neither uniqueness nor the general curvature >=-1 realization problem.
proof_architecture: Collapse each complementary component to obtain a topological sphere X and compact totally disconnected dust B. Smooth dust-disk covers give nested physical compact cores. Coordinates have finite Dirichlet energy, counting-l2 band budgets and possibly one exact additive period; compatibility(P) excludes free dust contacts of later levels with nondegenerate continua in generic earlier finite level unions.

For finitely many tests, independently shifted fine staircases preserve periods and agree with originals on a core. Their pairwise wedge integrals have small expectation. The expected number J of terminal grid collisions satisfies h^2 E J -> 0 by l2 dominated convergence. Compatibility permits the remaining dust to be covered by filling disks whose collars have at most one active coordinate. Fill there with differential rank <=1.

Choose A=sum du_i* tensor du_i* and regularize g_tau=A+tau g_0 outside the core. The summed energy density tends to 2 sqrt(det A), bounded by twice the sum of pairwise wedge magnitudes by Cauchy–Binet; rank-one filling regions contribute zero in the limit. Interpolate in a thin collar to retain the original metric near the core. Finite uniformization and exterior area-theorem bounds yield normalized limits and one complementary continuum K_b(f) for each dust label, with each followed round disk D_b contained in K_b(f).

Build compatible barriers from lower bounds on repeated-visit transboundary path costs. Tags preserve paths that run in earlier level sets; residual dust incidences obey constraints against earlier path laws and levels after finite deletions. Collar splicing and shrinking-jump removal retain cost lower bounds. A clipped chain distance has pointwise band widths <=4m and W^{1,2} control; shrinking positive smoothing preserves bands and free traces. A null-image criterion proves compatibility.

If no small barrier exists, pointwise modulus duality yields a law with L2 mean arclength density, l2 expected visit counts on prescribed countable sets, and absolutely continuous tag-tuple laws. Weighted tag slots can be moved later to make an auxiliary tuple cost arbitrarily small. Uniform bounds for every countable subset and atomless dust measure are fused into one whole-dust l2 hit-probability bound through finite separated-point tests, nonsmall closed sets, joint upper semicontinuity, and nested robust mixtures.

The residual/tag incidence constraints eliminate diffuse intersections of independent laws. Four paths with alternating collar starts must cross, while localized L2 occupations and l2 hit tails make their intersection probability small. Hence at most countably many endpoints lack small barriers. A maximal countable persistent barrier selection, followed by a parallel-line payment estimate, collapses every unmarked K_b to a point.

For a marked end, an unavailable local barrier gives a compact simple-arc law deep near that end. Average the integer indices of lifted rays to obtain a period-one coordinate with small energy and nonsingular bands. Its boundary derivative is the positive start distribution of total mass one. A putative protrusion away from D_b forces a fixed positive boundary integral, but a Stokes estimate bounds it by small energy and nonsingular l2 oscillations. Each test excludes an open neighborhood of one bad pair (f,D_b). Second countability permits countably many compatible persistent exclusions covering all bad pairs, so D_b=K_b. Retained original tests survive the selections and final finite transfers.

construction_ideas.idea: Separate a rigid core from a flexible completion, and reduce the completion to rank one before optimizing a quadratic cost.
construction_ideas.precise_hypotheses: A finite compatible coordinate family on a two-dimensional conformal domain has finite energies and counting-l2 band budgets. The original metric and coordinate values must be retained only near an exhausting core; outside that core a new smooth conformal structure may be chosen. Compatibility supplies filling collars with at most one nonconstant staircase coordinate.
construction_ideas.mechanism: Independent staircase shifts control pairwise wedge expectation and make h sqrt(J) small. Filling regions have rank(A)<=1 for A=sum du_i tensor du_i. With g_tau=A+tau g_0 the summed energy tends to 2 sqrt(det A)=2 sqrt(sum_{i<j}|du_i wedge du_j|^2). Thus near rank-one structure, rather than the individual derivative sizes in the original metric, controls the optimized quadratic cost. Core agreement is recovered by thin-collar interpolation.
construction_ideas.possible_bridge: Speculative: in a determinant construction, first freeze a witness block or common-basis minor and alter only auxiliary columns/rows outside it. Try to arrange low rank or low pairwise exterior products in the auxiliary region before bounding a quadratic occupancy cost. The Cauchy–Binet identity suggests investigating whether an occupancy relaxation can be expressed through exterior products while the nonzero witness remains fixed.
construction_ideas.missing_step: The source is specific to two-dimensional flexible metrics. Q(Z) row-transversals and integer determinants have a fixed coefficient geometry, and a metric change does not preserve an integer-height estimate. One must exhibit an allowed discrete operation preserving the chosen minor and the BA lower bound, with a proved effect on actual column cost; no such operation follows from this paper.

construction_ideas.idea: Charge every visit with multiplicity, but keep hit probabilities and expected visit counts as separate invariants.
construction_ideas.precise_hypotheses: Allowed paths have finite domain-part length, density g in L2 and nonnegative counting-l2 boundary toll m. A toll is charged at every parameter time, not merely at each distinct point. Cutting/concatenation is permitted only with countably many new junction/limit times and finite resulting domain-part length. Endpoint toll omissions are explicitly recorded.
construction_ideas.mechanism: Repeated-visit cost is additive under disjoint time decomposition; collar splicing and shrinking-jump removal pay exactly one toll at each merged junction without duplicating cut tolls. In laws, mean counts n_mu are controlled on specified countable sets for products such as sum m_xi n_mu, whereas hit probabilities m_mu are controlled on the whole dust for intersection bounds. The proof never substitutes a distinct-hit bound for a multiplicity bound.
construction_ideas.possible_bridge: Speculative: annotate each row/column or common-basis operation with its occurrence count, and distinguish support occupancy from total multiplicity before applying an l2/Cauchy–Schwarz estimate. This may expose where a row-transversal argument pays a column several times and where a quadratic occupancy sum is actually required. A decomposition that counts junctions once could prevent accidental loss in determinant height accounting.
construction_ideas.missing_step: There is no determinant or matroid statement here. A path-time charge is linear; the project's quadratic occupancy penalty must be derived from an explicit discrete count vector and cannot be inferred from the law's l2 hit norm. The countability/finite-length hypotheses are indispensable for the source concatenation theorem.

source_anchors.label: Positive laws: hit probabilities versus expected visit counts

construction_ideas.idea: Turn separate countable feasibility tests into one common object by requiring robust neighborhood bounds before every later mixture.
construction_ideas.precise_hypotheses: A Borel family M of laws is closed under all Borel probability mixtures. It admits a Polish topology with the same Borel sets, and m_z(s) is jointly upper semicontinuous on M times compact metric B. For every countable D and finite atomless lambda, some law has ||m_z|D||_2<=C0 and integral m_z d lambda=0, uniformly in D and lambda.
construction_ideas.mechanism: The failures of prescribed tests form a sigma-ideal. Within a closed nonsmall set, remove basis-open small pieces. On finite r-separated configurations, minimax produces a finite mixture meeting all dual weighted l2 tests. Joint upper semicontinuity makes that estimate hold for every simultaneous choice in small closed child neighborhoods. Nested finite branching with shrinking diameters produces a mixture of branch limits that retains every earlier neighborhood estimate. Sending r to zero controls every finite subset of B and hence counting-l2(B).
construction_ideas.possible_bridge: Speculative: this is a precise warning against proving each rank/cost constraint using a different basis and then declaring a common basis exists. For a common-basis search one could first ask whether a convex family of candidate distributions has uniform tests and a topology making their feasibility robust, then maintain all old finite constraints under later choices. Even a finite analogue may help separate a fractional common distribution from an actual witness.
construction_ideas.missing_step: The law output is a mixture, not a deterministic integral basis or row-transversal. Full rank is not convex under averaging matrices, and a determinant may cancel. To use it, one needs either distributions on already valid common bases plus an integral rounding theorem preserving the quadratic cost, or another noncancellation argument. Countable tests alone are insufficient without the stated atomless tests, mixture closure, and joint upper semicontinuity.

construction_ideas.idea: Preserve an existing budget through positive-excess bounds, and make every new obstruction test survive all later extensions.
construction_ideas.precise_hypotheses: Each fixed coordinate has a counting-l2 band budget a_i; every finite transfer has distinct terminal indices and positive-excess error ||[A_i-a_i]_+||_2<epsilon. Original coordinates and periods are retained exactly on exhausting cores. Compatibility is formulated through finite earlier sublists, so flags may grow and countable limit unions preserve it. Bad limiting pairs live in a second-countable parameter space and admit local exclusion by one fixed appended test.
construction_ideas.mechanism: Minkowski gives ||A_i||_2<=||a_i||_2+epsilon without summing the old budget again at every stage. Fixed tests are eventually present in all finite sublists, even when the well-order exceeds omega. Their contradiction uses fixed compact source sets and vanishing transfer errors, so later list extensions cannot invalidate an earlier exclusion. Each strict open enlargement consumes a new countable-basis element, giving a countable selection covering all bad pairs.
construction_ideas.possible_bridge: Speculative: retain a verified nonzero minor or rank certificate exactly, record only incremental positive cost excess, and require later row/column additions to preserve that certificate. For a compact normalized family of possible counterexamples, local robust determinant/cost contradictions could potentially be organized into a persistent finite or countable test family. This highlights the quantifier gap between a witness depending on each test and one construction surviving every test.
construction_ideas.missing_step: A nonzero polynomial minor is an open condition after evaluation, but fixed-height integer points need not form a compact parameter family and countable selection is not a finite determinant construction. One must supply a discrete persistence lemma, quantitative nonvanishing margin and height control. Positive-excess estimates cannot replace a missing lower bound for the chosen integer determinant.

construction_ideas.idea: Build the lower and upper bounds from the same fixed normalized functional, isolating a unit topological charge from all small costs.
construction_ideas.precise_hypotheses: A compact family of simple arcs runs from a smooth collar to one dust end. The mean occupation has L2 density, nonsingular hit probabilities have counting-l2 norm, and prior-level intersections are integrable with free contacts excluded. Averaging lifted integer ray indices yields a continuous period-one coordinate with a positive boundary derivative measure of total mass one; smoothing preserves period and bands.
construction_ideas.mechanism: Gate the arc starts a distance d0>0 from a candidate round disk. The same boundary integral of dist(f(.),D) du is >=d0 before smoothing, remains >d0/2 nearby, and is <=sqrt(pi)L||du||_2+2pi L||a off singularity||_2 under Stokes. Deep localization makes the upper bound <d0/4. The distinguished singularity has budget and period one but disappears from the upper-bound error because dist(.,D)=0 on its disk.
construction_ideas.possible_bridge: Speculative: the determinant project likewise needs upper and lower estimates for the identical integer object. Seek a normalized discrete charge or cofactor pairing equal to a fixed nonzero integer, and arrange for the expensive distinguished part to be annihilated by the test functional, leaving only small error contributions. This is a construction pattern for targeting a contradiction, not an arithmetic conclusion about pi.
construction_ideas.missing_step: The source's unit charge is winding number and its cancellation is a distance function vanishing on one disk. There is no provided integer matrix, BA estimate, or arithmetic analogue cancelling a high-cost column. Any proposed cofactor functional must be proved integral, nonzero, and compatible with the actual coefficient-height and occupancy accounting.

limits: This is a complete first reading of the pinned source, not independent verification of the asserted solution to Koebe's conjecture. No external cited proof was checked and no PDF compilation or page-by-page PDF comparison was performed.

The source explicitly permits changing the conformal structure outside the retained cores. It does not establish convergence for arbitrary original-domain exhaustions merely from finite uniformization.

Finite transfers preserve arbitrarily selected finite ordered sublists; they are not required to be finite initial segments of a countable ordinal. Later compatibility/flag extensions preserve fixed tests, but compatibility(P) is a genuine hypothesis, not automatic for arbitrary appended functions.

The fusion output controls whole-dust hit probabilities, while mean visit counts are controlled only on designated countable sets. Confusing these conclusions would lose the residual-intersection estimates.

The hyperbolic corollary assumes curvature identically -1, includes a metric-double convention for planar hulls, and states neither uniqueness nor a prescribed ideal-boundary extension. General curvature at least -1 is explicitly left separate.

No result here proves Q(Z) row rank, common integral bases, an integer determinant lower/upper contradiction, or the needed arithmetic height versus quadratic-occupancy balance. All proposed transfers are speculative and have explicit missing steps.
